target_customer: Quantitative teams in finance, insurance, consumer goods and ML groups that need to tune models and experiments
problem: Tuning model parameters and experiments by grid or random search wastes compute and time; SigOpt offered Bayesian optimization as an API.
business_model: Usage and seat based SaaS and API subscriptions

founders.name: Scott Clark
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no bio. Press on the Intel deal says he built the framework from his Cornell research; that is not recorded as education because the article was not opened.

founders.name: Patrick Hayes
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in search results of the a16z announcement and as CTO in Intel coverage; neither opened, YC page lists only Clark.

technical_complexity.rationale: Bayesian optimization at scale as a reliable hosted service demanded applied mathematics and distributed systems, built on the open source MOE project.

defensibility.rationale: Algorithms were published research and open source alternatives existed, so the moat was execution and integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Intel acquired SigOpt in 2020 to extend its AI software; Whetlab was bought by Twitter per outside knowledge only, not sourced here.

market_need_then: Machine learning adoption was rising and early customers in consumer goods and finance used SigOpt to tune experiments, including a shaving cream formulation test (TechCrunch Feb 2015).

branding.domain_note: sigopt.com; now redirects through Intel's corporate redirector.
branding.community_and_virality: Sponsored academic and ML community events; no brand-focused press found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known among ML practitioners but sources show no brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: SigOpt turned Bayesian optimization research into an API, raised about 8.6 million dollars across a 2015 a16z-backed seed and a 6.6 million dollar 2016 Series A, found customers in finance and consumer goods, and was acquired by Intel in October 2020 for undisclosed terms. Timing with machine learning adoption and a technical product explain the outcome.
notes: Seed amount of 2M comes from a VentureBeat headline and search summaries; the TechCrunch Series A article states date June 2015 but not the amount. Reported totals vary (8M, 8.8M, aggregator 9M across four rounds). The sigopt.com fetch was a redirect to Intel and was not followed. Competitor Whetlab dated by CB Insights founding year 2014 only; Spearmint and Hyperopt were found only in 2016 sources so are excluded. The takeover outcome field must not claim Whetlab fate; it was not sourced. Name origin not found.
